prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1497; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured's policy-named driver reported a sideswipe during a lane change on a multi-lane road. The claimant, who is not represented by counsel, was identified as a passenger in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses place the claimant in the vehicle at the moment of impact. The other driver's account matches the claimant's description of how the collision happened.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene were received and show contact damage on the passenger side that lines up with the reported impact point. No prior damage to the vehicle appears in our records or the photos.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection completed. The damage pattern is consistent with a sideswipe at the reported angle and speed, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 5: Claimant reported neck and back strain and was seen at an urgent care clinic the same day. Clinic notes describe pain and stiffness that fit the mechanism of this type of collision.

Entry 6: Medical records show no earlier injury to the neck or back. Claimant has not reported prior treatment to those areas, and nothing in the file contradicts that.

Entry 7: Claimant gave a follow-up statement adding a few minor details, such as the exact lane positions and the sound of contact. The core account of the event has not changed from the first report.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course of physical therapy and home exercises. Pain reports have gradually decreased over the past several weeks as the claimant improved.

Entry 9: Treating provider's notes show steady progress with fewer visits needed as range of motion returned. Symptoms are consistent with the expected recovery timeline for soft tissue strain.

Entry 10: Reviewed the full file with the witness statements, scene photos, and police report. All sources agree on how the accident happened and on the claimant's presence in the vehicle.

Entry 11: Injury evaluation reviewed. The reported injury is plausible for a crash of this kind and the treatment is reasonable for the diagnosis.

Entry 12: Claim is ready for settlement review. Recommend the file proceed to evaluation of medical costs and vehicle repair estimate with no coverage issues identified.
